3. Eventually, the learned Judge of the Adalat by the Judgment and decree dated 15-2-2005 decreed the suit on contest against the defendant No. 6 Bashirullah (herein petitioner) and ex parte against others. 

 4. The decree holder bank then put the decree in execution in Artha Rin Execution Case No. 28 of 2005. As the mortgaged property was diluvated into the river, so, on the prayer of the decree holder bank, the adalat by the order dated 13-11-2005 issued warrant of arrest against the petitioner, fixing 30-11- 2005 for service return. 

 8. Mr Mohammad Ali, the learned Advocate appearing for the respondent No. 3 decree holder bank, opposes the Rule and submits that section 34 of the Ain 2003 is a measure to realise debt from defaulting borrowers. He adds that there is no illegality in the impugned order which calls for no interference by this Court. 

 10. On going to the materials on record, it transpires to us that as the mortgaged property was diluvated into the river, so the decree holder bank was not in a position to sell the property in auction, and, as such, on the prayer of the bank, the Adalat by the order dated 13-11-2005 issued warrant of arrest pursuant to the provisions of section 34(1) of the Ain 2003 to compel the judgment debtor petitioner for payment of decretal amount. We failed to discover any illegality in the impugned order. Moreover, we find that the impugned order dated 13-11-2005 in its entirety are well founded in the facts and circumstances of the case. So, the grounds urged and contentions advanced by the learned Counsel for the petitioner are not the correct exposition of law and facts.
